class Config:
    def __init__(self):
        self.settings = {
            'database_url': 'sqlite:///config.db',
            'encryption_key': b'your_secret_key',  # Replace with a secure key in production
            'logging_level': 'INFO'
        }

    @staticmethod
    def get_db_connection():
        import sqlite3
        return sqlite3.connect(Config.settings['database_url'])

    def load_settings(self):
        try:
            conn = self.get_db_connection()
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            query = """
                INSERT OR REPLACE INTO config_data (setting, value) VALUES (?, ?)
                ON CONFLICT SET value = ?;
            """
            cursor.execute(query, ('db_url', Config.settings['database_url'], Config.settings['database_url']))
            cursor.execute(query, ('encryption_key', Config.settings['encryption_key'], Config.settings['encryption_key']))
            cursor.execute(query, ('logging_level', Config.settings['logging_level'], Config.settings['logging_level']))
            conn.commit()
        except Exception as e:
            raise f"Failed to load settings: {e}"
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_setting(self, name):
        import sqlite3
        conn = self.get_db_connection()
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        query = "SELECT value FROM config_data WHERE setting = ?"
        current_value = cursor.execute(query, (name,)).fetchone()[0]
        conn.close()
        return current_value

    def update_settings(self, settings):
        try:
            conn = self.get_db_connection()
            for key, val in settings.items():
                if key == 'encryption_key':
                    import os
                    val = os.urandom(32)  # Replace with actual secure key generation method in production
                self.set_setting(key, val)
            conn.commit()
        except Exception as e:
            raise f"Failed to update settings: {e}"
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def set_setting(self, name, value):
        import sqlite3
        conn = self.get_db_connection()
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        query = "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO config_data (setting, value) VALUES (?, ?)"
        cursor.execute(query, (name, value))
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

    def delete_setting(self, name):
        import sqlite3
        conn = self.get_db_connection()
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        query = "DELETE FROM config_data WHERE setting = ?"
        cursor.execute(query, (name,))
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

name: full 3d chess game

data.label: ui_screens
data.description: Chess UI: renders the 8x8 board with pieces, legal-move highlighting, status banner, move log, Reset/Undo buttons and a '3D Board' toggle with a perspective-projected canvas view. Exports render() as the app entry.

data.label: core_engine
data.description: App controller: ChessEngine facade (select/move/reset/undo/status) and InputHandler that wires DOM squares to the engine with click-to-select then click-to-move. Re-exports engine types for siblings.

data.label: input_handler
data.description: Keyboard control: arrow keys move a cursor, Enter/Space selects a piece then plays the move, Escape cancels. Works alongside the mouse InputHandler.

data.label: data_store
data.description: Game state store: owns the board, turn, move history, selection and game status; wraps the rules engine (game_engine) and exposes the shared chessEngine singleton plus addMove/updateBoard/detectCheckmate API. Supports undo via snapshots.

data.label: game_engine

name: void raider

data.label: void_raider blueprint
data.description: void raider
data.appGoal: void raider
data.appPurpose: Classic top-down arcade space shooter in the tradition of Asteroids and Space Invaders. The player pilots a ship with thrust and rotation controls (Arrow keys/WASD) and fires projectiles with Space. Waves of enemy raider ships descend from the top in escalating formations — each wave has more enemies, moving faster with more HP (count-based spawning, roughly 18 seconds per wave). Enemies drift downward and re-enter from the top at random columns; hitting an enemy costs 1 HP. Player projectiles travel along the ship heading; collisions use simple distance checks. Scoring: 100 points per enemy destroyed. The player has 100 HP and 3 lives; enemy contact deals damage, losing all HP costs a life, and the game ends at 0 lives (R restarts). Renders on an 800x600 canvas in a neon vector style (green ship, red enemies, yellow projectiles) with a HUD showing SCORE, LIVES, and WAVE.
